walkthroughs.body_html:
A circuit is a loop where charge can flow. ⚡

Current is how much charge flows per second. It is measured in amperes (A) using an ammeter, which goes in series.

Voltage (also called potential difference) is the energy each unit of charge carries. It is measured in volts (V) using a voltmeter, placed in parallel across a component.

Resistance is how much a component opposes the current. It is measured in ohms (Ω).

Thin wires, long wires, and hot wires all have more resistance. Thick, short, cool wires have less resistance.

A resistor is a component made to have a fixed resistance.

Ohm's law: V = I × R. If V doubles and R stays the same, I doubles too.

In a series circuit there is one loop. The current is the same at every point, but voltage is shared between components.

In a parallel circuit there are branches. Each branch sees the full voltage, but the current splits.

mcqs.q: Which instrument measures current, and how is it connected?
options: Voltmeter, in parallel
Ammeter, in series
Ammeter, in parallel
Voltmeter, in series

mcqs.q: In a series circuit with one battery and two bulbs, what is true about the current?
options: It is largest near the battery
It is the same everywhere
It splits between the bulbs
It is zero in one bulb

mcqs.q: What happens to the total resistance when you add another resistor in parallel?
options: Voltage measures how many electrons are stored in a battery.
Total resistance decreases — there are more paths for current to flow.
Adding any resistor always increases the total resistance.
Adding a parallel resistor doubles the voltage available.

mcqs.q: What happens to the current as it goes around a series circuit?
options: Current gets used up by each component as it flows around the circuit.
Voltage measures how many electrons are stored in a battery.
Current splits in half at the battery so each direction gets some.
It stays the same at every point — current is conserved.

mcqs.q: What does voltage (potential difference) across a component represent?
options: The energy transferred per unit charge passing through that component.
Voltage measures how many electrons are stored in a battery.
Voltage is the 'amount of electricity' flowing through the wire.
Adding a parallel resistor doubles the voltage available.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Parallel circuit”?
options: Energy per unit charge, measured in volts (V)
Branches in a loop — each branch shares the voltage
Opposition to current, measured in ohms (Ω)
V = I × R for ohmic conductors at fixed temperature
